title: Query Sources: Where, Return, Let, and Sort
description: CQL queries are the workhorse of data extraction: [Resource] alias where / return / sort by clauses, let bindings for computed intermediates, singleton from for exactly-one extractions, and Tuple construction for shaped results.
learningObjectives: Filter with where and compose Boolean conditions
Extract exactly-one results with singleton from
Combine retrieves with union and deduplicate with distinct

hints.message: Count([Observation] O where O.status = 'final') — alias O binds each row.
Max(...) over a return projection: [Observation] O where O.valueQuantity.value is not null return O.valueQuantity.value.
Avg([Observation] O return O.valueQuantity.value) — (120 + 138 + 13.5) / 3 = 90.5 for Alice.
First([Observation] O sort by (O.effective as FHIR.dateTime) return O.id) — sort by the choice-type effective, cast to FHIR.dateTime.
singleton from (query) returns the single element or errors if the result doesn't have exactly one item — obs-2's 138 for Alice.
Tuple { id: O.id, status: O.status } builds a structured value; the result renders as JSON.
Count(distinct (query)) deduplicates the projected values — Alice has final + preliminary = 2.
let isBP: O.code.coding.code contains '8488-6'... careful: the LOINC code here is 8480-6. let names a per-row intermediate you can reuse in where/return.
Compose conditions with and: O.status = 'final' and O.valueQuantity.value > 100 — only obs-2 (138) qualifies, but it's preliminary! So 0... wait, is it? obs-1 is 120 and final — so 1.
[Observation] union [Condition] combines retrieves before Count — Alice has 3 obs + 1 condition = 4.
